title: OpenAI Dots Alternatives: 10 Compared (2026)
summary: OpenAI Dots alternatives for anyone priced out of ChatGPT dots at $100 or locked out in the EEA and UK: Marblism from $24/mo, Grok Bot at $20/mo, OpenClaw free.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** The best OpenAI Dots alternatives are Marblism, Grok Bot and OpenClaw. For small-business owners who want roles handled start to finish, Marblism gives you 7 AI Employees from $24 a month on the yearly plan and that is my pick. Grok Bot is the closest hosted match at $20 a month: a cloud agent on a cloud computer that keeps going after you close the tab. If you want the agent off everyone's cloud, OpenClaw is free and runs on your own machine. And if you are in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland on a Pro plan, dots is off the table, but most of the tools below are not.


OpenAI started rolling out dots on September 29, and if you are on a Pro plan in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, you cannot have one. If you are anywhere else, the cheapest plan that includes a dot is $100 a month.


## What OpenAI Dots is and what it costs


So what is a dot, in plain terms? It is an AI agent that lives inside your ChatGPT account, which is why you will also see it called ChatGPT dots. OpenAI gives it its own computer in the cloud, and it keeps working on whatever you handed it after you walk away: it reads, researches, drafts, and pings you in ChatGPT, Slack or Teams when it needs a decision. OpenAI's[launch post](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/) puts it as "an always-on agent inside ChatGPT that takes on ongoing responsibility". The first dot comes free with a Pro or Business Premium plan, and talking to it does not eat your ChatGPT limits.


The pricing tiers that include a dot:


What OpenAI Dots is and what it costs Plan Price What you get


Pro 100, 200 and 500 $100, $200 and $500/mo Dots in eligible markets


Business Premium $100/seat/mo (annual, 2-seat workspace minimum) Dots across all supported ChatGPT regions, 5x more usage than Standard, no 5-hour limit


Enterprise Admin-enabled beta Dots when workspace admin enables it


If you are outside those regions and can spend $100 a month, dots is available to you. The rollout is gradual and not open to users under 18. If either condition does not hold, the alternatives below are the path, unless Business Premium fits you: $100 a seat a month billed annually ($125 monthly), a workspace of at least 2 seats, so $120 a month at the least, and dots in every supported region.


Three reactions from the first week stuck with me. Once an agent holds your integrations and your work history, leaving gets harder. That is the real lock-in here. Nobody in those early threads named something a dot does that OpenClaw, Hermes or Muse cannot. And Pro users in Europe found out from the help page that they are not invited.


## Which OpenAI Dots alternative for which problem


Eight situations bring people here. The right tool depends on which one is yours.


Which OpenAI Dots alternative for which problem Situation Tool Entry price


Locked out as a Pro user in the EEA, UK or Switzerland OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, OpenDots, Grok Bot, Lindy, Claude Cowork, Perplexity Computer, Marblism Free to $24/mo


Priced out below $100/mo All 10: Marblism, Grok Bot, Meta Muse, Perplexity Computer, Gemini Spark, Claude Cowork, Lindy, OpenDots, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw $0 to $24/mo


Want business roles handled, not an agent to direct Marblism from $24/mo (yearly)


Want a persistent cloud agent with a browser and a filesystem Grok Bot From $20/mo (Cursor Pro)


Want a free personal agent in the US or Canada Meta Muse Free for most use


Want full hardware control, no subscription OpenClaw, Hermes Agent Free


Want research with citations in every output Perplexity Computer From $20/mo (Pro)


Want document and file work handed off Claude Cowork From $17/mo (Pro, annual)


## What the alternatives already offer that dots do not


### Eight OpenAI Dots alternatives are available in Europe and the UK


Pro users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK cannot use dots. Business Premium lifts that restriction, but it is a team product: $100 per seat per month billed annually and a 2-seat workspace, so at least $120 a month.


For Pro users in those regions, the practical alternatives are the self-hosted tools (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, OpenDots) and Marblism, Grok Bot, Lindy, Claude Cowork and Perplexity Computer, none of which state a region restriction on their own pages. The other two are out: Meta Muse is US and Canada only, and Gemini Spark is not offered in these regions.


### Every OpenAI Dots alternative here starts below $100 a month


Everything on this list starts below a dot's $100. Most of it a lot lower. Each tool's pricing is in its own Pricing block below.


### Four OpenAI Dots alternatives let you choose the model


Every dot runs on GPT-6 Astra. If the model matters to you, Perplexity Computer picks the best model for each query from GPT, Gemini, Claude and NVIDIA Nemotron, and lets you set a preferred one. Hermes Agent supports any OpenAI-compatible provider, switchable with one command. OpenDots takes any OpenAI-compatible model provider. OpenClaw swaps models and agent plugins the same way. Those 4 are the most direct answer if model flexibility is what you need.


### Self-hosted OpenAI Dots alternatives keep your data on your hardware


Each dot has its own cloud computer with sandboxed environments on OpenAI's infrastructure. An always-on agent that holds your integrations and work history is essentially your computer in the cloud. The lock-in that comes with that is real: the longer it runs on a given platform, the harder switching becomes.


Self-hosted tools are the clean answer. OpenClaw stores state, memory, and credentials on your own hardware. Models are plugins you swap without changing anything else. Hermes Agent keeps conversations, memory, and skills locally in` ~/.hermes/` . OpenDots is a self-hosted template you run yourself, though conversations require CopilotKit Intelligence.


### Three OpenAI Dots alternatives were in public use before dots launched


Dots began rolling out on September 29. Grok Bot launched August 11, and OpenClaw has built up 391.5k GitHub stars. Hermes Agent has 251.8k. OpenDots was announced October 1, so it is as new as dots.


In dots' first week, one early user reported the cloud machine dying multiple times with no support for preview links, while competing tools handled similar workloads end to end. A tool with months of public use behind it carries less of that risk.


## How to choose an OpenAI Dots alternative


There are 3 tracks. Pick the one that matches how much you want to operate the thing yourself, and the right tools become obvious.


How to choose an OpenAI Dots alternative Done-for-you Managed agent Self-hosted


Who owns the output The role owner (an AI Employee) You direct, agent executes You own everything


What you operate daily Approve before send Set goals, review results Configure, maintain server


What happens when you stop paying Roles stop. Output you approved stays Varies by maker. Gemini Spark pauses schedules and removes access. Lindy keeps the workspace active to the end of the paid cycle. Grok Bot, Perplexity, Claude Cowork and Meta Muse do not publish what happens. Your install stays on your hardware (OpenDots conversations still need CopilotKit Intelligence)


Who can pick up the work Any team member on the account You Anyone with server access


Matching tools Marblism Grok Bot, Perplexity Computer, Gemini Spark, Lindy, Claude Cowork, Meta Muse OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, OpenDots


Left to right is how much of the work stays with you: Marblism is the only tool here where you hand off a role instead of directing an agent or running a server.


### Done-for-you OpenAI Dots alternatives: AI Employees that own a role


On this track, an AI Employee owns a role. It works toward that role, surfaces anything that needs your approval, and no action goes out without your say-so. You are handing off a function, not directing an agent toward a goal. Marblism is the tool for this track.


### Managed-agent OpenAI Dots alternatives: cloud agents you direct


You set a goal, the agent works in the cloud, and you review the result. The agent connects to your tools. Grok Bot, Claude Cowork, Meta Muse and Gemini Spark also give it a browser. Gemini Spark works natively in Gmail, Calendar and Drive. Grok Bot records workflows and runs them on its own. Perplexity backs every answer with sources. Lindy is where I'd go if event-triggered workflows across many tools are what you need.


### Self-hosted OpenAI Dots alternatives: agents on your own hardware


Your data stays on hardware you control, with one exception: OpenDots conversations run through CopilotKit Intelligence. You are responsible for setup and maintenance. OpenClaw keeps state, memory and credentials on your hardware. Hermes Agent stores conversations, memory and skills locally. OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and OpenDots are the tools here. Setup varies: OpenClaw installs with a one-liner, Hermes Agent has a desktop app for macOS and Windows, and OpenDots needs Node.js 24 and npm.


## 10 best OpenAI Dots alternatives in 2026


Start at the top if you want work handled rather than directed. The managed agents come next, and the list ends with the three you host yourself. Each block closes with a direct comparison to OpenAI Dots.


### 1. Marblism: OpenAI Dots alternative with 7 AI Employees for business roles


If you want a business role handled start to finish rather than an agent you aim at goals,[Marblism](https://www.marblism.com/) is the place to start. You get all 7 AI Employees on every plan:[Eva](https://www.marblism.com/ai-employees/eva) (executive assistant),[Sonny](https://www.marblism.com/ai-employees/sonny) (social media),[Stan](https://www.marblism.com/ai-employees/stan) (lead generation),[Penny](https://www.marblism.com/ai-employees/penny) (SEO and content),[Rachel](https://www.marblism.com/ai-employees/rachel) (receptionist),[Walter](https://www.marblism.com/ai-employees/walter) (website builder) and[Linda](https://www.marblism.com/ai-employees/linda) (legal assistant). They run off one record of the business, so a lead Rachel qualifies is already in front of Stan when he follows up, and in front of Eva when she prepares the meeting.


Nothing is sent, posted, signed or called without your approval. You get 50 hours of AI work per month, reset monthly, spent only on advanced actions. Chat and quick tasks don't touch the clock.


#### Key Features


- All 7 AI Employees included on every plan, each owning its own business role
- Shared context across the whole team: one record, not siloed agents
- Your approval is required before any action goes out
- 50 hours of AI work a month, reset monthly, with top-ups available
- Rachel supports local phone numbers in the US, Canada, the UK, Mexico and Australia, answers in multiple languages, and syncs with Google and Outlook calendars
- Stan connects to a 700M+ leads database and runs email and LinkedIn outreach once you approve it


#### Pros


- Flat-rate pricing with unlimited team members and unlimited businesses per account
- Chat and quick tasks don't consume hours. Only advanced actions draw down the 50 monthly hours
- Approval-before-send model removes the risk of an agent acting without your sign-off
- Trusted by over 40,000 businesses


#### Cons


- No free plan or free trial. Entry is through a paid subscription with a 7-day money-back window. On the yearly plan the entry rate is $24 a month ($288 up front), while the monthly plan is $44 a month


#### Pricing


- [$24/mo](https://www.marblism.com/pricing) (yearly, billed $288 up front), all 7 AI Employees, 50 hours/mo, unlimited seats and businesses
- **$33/mo** (quarterly), same features
- **$44/mo** (monthly), same features
- 7-day money-back guarantee on all plans


#### User Reviews


Marblism holds a[4.8 out of 5 on Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/www.marblism.com) from 1,161 reviews. Users credit the breadth most: one account covers website building, social media, receptionist calls, lead outreach and content in parallel. Support comes up almost as often, usually with the support person thanked by first name.


> "Sonny runs 3 client social media accounts on autopilot, Penny writes SEO blogs for my personal brand, and Eva handles my emails… As a solo digital marketer, it's like having a writer, designer, and social manager in one platform."
>
>
> Faisal Saleh Hayat on[Marblism](https://www.marblism.com/)


#### Best For


I'd pick Marblism if you want a business function handled end to end, not walked through step by step. You're a solopreneur running social media, lead generation, inbox management and a receptionist line, and you'd rather approve the output than supervise the work. It is the closest you get to a team without the headcount.


**vs OpenAI Dots:** $24 a month on the yearly plan ($44 monthly) against $100 for the cheapest plan that includes a dot. Marblism's 7 AI Employees each own their own role, working from one shared business record. A dot is a generalist you direct. Every Marblism action waits for your sign-off.


---


### 2. Grok Bot: OpenAI Dots alternative with a persistent cloud agent and workflow recording


The closest hosted thing to a dot on this list is[Grok Bot](https://grok.com/) . Bots work on a computer in the cloud, sign into the tools you already use, finish jobs end to end, and only come back when something needs your approval. Where dots give each agent its own isolated machine, all your Grok bots share one persistent cloud computer, with isolation per user rather than per bot. That structure is what lets bots hand work off and keep context between them without you managing the handoff.


The workflow-recording feature is what makes Grok Bot worth a second look. Show a bot a workflow once, it saves it as a routine and runs it on its own next time. Bots run in parallel, 24/7, even when your laptop is closed.


#### Key Features


- Your bots share one persistent cloud computer with a browser, files and app logins
- Workflow recording: walk through a task once and the bot runs it on its own next time
- Parallel bots in a group thread pass work between themselves without your involvement
- Bots run 24/7 in the cloud, with apps for macOS, Windows, Linux and iOS
- Supports Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Slack and MCP servers
- Auto Review checks risky actions (shell commands, plugin calls, computer use) before they run


#### Pros


- Included on paid Cursor plans (Pro at $20/mo) and SuperGrok, so entry is well below dots' $100 floor
- Shared cloud computer lets bots collaborate and hand context off without starting over
- Workflow recording removes the need to re-describe a task you've done before
- 4.9 out of 5 on the App Store across a large review base


#### Cons


- On-demand token usage is the cost to watch: always-on agents draw on a lot of tokens, and enabling on-demand means charges can run past your weekly included allowance
- All bots share one cloud computer: a well-designed feature for handoffs, but it means isolation is per user, not per bot
- Linking a SuperGrok or X Premium+ subscription grants usage but doesn't stack on top of an existing Cursor plan that already includes Grok Bot
- Legacy, request-based Cursor pricing requires opting into usage-based pricing before Grok Bot is available


#### Pricing


- [$20/mo](https://grok.com/plans) (Cursor Pro, billed monthly), Grok Bot access with weekly usage included
- **$30/mo** (SuperGrok, billed monthly), Grok Bot with weekly usage
- **$25/mo** ($300/year, SuperGrok annual), lower annual rate
- On-demand usage available when weekly included usage runs out, billed through Cursor


#### User Reviews


Grok Bot holds a[4.9 out of 5 on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/grok-bot/id6794501026?see-all=reviews&platform=iphone) from 9.5K ratings. Most users run several bots, one each for email, a business function, subscriptions and personal tasks. What they mention most is that the background work that used to slip through the cracks now gets done.


> "[This is by far](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/grok-bot/id6794501026?see-all=reviews&platform=iphone) one of the most helpful useful and user-friendly AI applications out there. If you procrastinate or there's certain things that you struggle to get done or you carry a large cognitive load with all the different things going on in your life, this app will relieve that burden and help you succeed in all those areas as well as make you feel superhuman."
>
>
> User on[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/grok-bot/id6794501026?see-all=reviews&platform=iphone)


#### Best For


I'd pick Grok Bot if you want a cloud agent that runs workflows on its own and you're already in the Cursor or SuperGrok ecosystem. You want dots-level always-on behaviour without the $100 Pro floor, and you're comfortable with token-based usage as the cost model. For more cloud agents at this price point, see[our Grok Bot alternatives guide](https://www.marblism.com/blog/grok-bot-alternatives) .


**vs OpenAI Dots:** Both give you a persistent cloud agent that runs 24/7 and connects to tools. The difference is ecosystem: dots lives in ChatGPT's plugin network. Grok Bot lives in Cursor's ecosystem, and bots share one cloud computer rather than each getting an isolated one. Cursor Pro at $20/mo is a fifth of dots' entry.


---


### 3. Meta Muse: free OpenAI Dots alternative for the US and Canada


Close the app and Muse keeps going. It runs on Muse Secure VM, a dedicated virtual machine with its own browser, and it returns when something changes or needs your approval, whether that's before it sends an email or makes a purchase. It's available in the US and Canada, free for most use, and Meta says it is the first AI agent covered by Stripe Link's purchase protections, including free coverage for damaged or lost items, price drops and no-fee returns.


Muse is powered by Muse Spark, Meta's most capable model, and doesn't share your conversations or VM data with Meta's ad systems.


#### Key Features


- Runs on a dedicated, isolated Muse Secure VM in the cloud with its own browser
- Continues working after you close the app. Returns when approval is needed
- Checkout via Stripe Link with purchase protections: free coverage for damaged items, price drops, no-fee returns
- Sentinel agent runs on the same VM, kept apart at the system level, and approves every outbound action
- Available on iOS, Android and muse.ai. Computer use on Mac lets Muse drive any app
- Supports custom connectors plus 15+ third-party tools including Slack, Shopify, Notion and QuickBooks


#### Pros


- Free for most personal use
- Meta says Muse is the first AI agent covered by Stripe Link's purchase protections
- Muse has no visibility into your passwords or payment methods. Credentials go into secure storage
- Muse Confidential VM is coming, where the whole VM is encrypted with a key only you hold


#### Cons


- Available in the US and Canada. Readers outside those markets will need another option from this list
- Free tier has token limits. Heavy use requires a paid plan


#### Pricing


- **Free** : most personal use, limited tokens
- [$20/mo](https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/) , Power plan, 500M Muse tokens per week
- **$100/mo** : Maximum plan, 3B Muse tokens per week


#### User Reviews


Muse holds a[4.9 out of 5 on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/muse-from-meta/id6760173601?see-all=reviews&platform=iphone) from 204K ratings. Users keep coming back to how proactive it is: it messages you first, not the other way around. The common experience is someone who expected a chatbot and found it picking up their subscriptions, clearing their inbox, and connecting to their bank and social accounts in the first session.


> "[She also messages me](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/muse-from-meta/id6760173601?see-all=reviews&platform=iphone) to remind me of things I was thinking of starting or makes suggestions of things I might want to try to help my life. Offering all of this help while having conversations like two humans would have."
>
>
> User on[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/muse-from-meta/id6760173601?see-all=reviews&platform=iphone)


#### Best For


I'd pick Muse if you're in the US or Canada and want a personal agent that handles real tasks, browses the web, makes purchases with protections, and doesn't share your data with ad systems. Start free and decide whether $20 a month is worth it from there. See[our Muse alternatives guide](https://www.marblism.com/blog/muse-alternatives) for more personal agent options.


**vs OpenAI Dots:** Muse is free to start. Muse runs on Meta's VM. Dots runs on OpenAI's cloud.


---


### 4. Perplexity Computer: OpenAI Dots alternative with cited research and multi-model selection


When cited research needs to be baked into every output, no other tool on this list matches what[Perplexity Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/) delivers. Where a dot runs on one model, Perplexity Computer orchestrates multiple models, including GPT, Gemini, Claude and NVIDIA Nemotron, and selects the best one per query. Every answer comes with its sources.


Computer is available on Pro and Max subscribers on desktop, mobile, Slack and Microsoft 365. It runs tasks asynchronously in the background, supports scheduled recurring jobs, and uses domain-specific sub-agents for market research, financial analysis and news monitoring.


#### Key Features


- Multi-model selection: orchestrates GPT, Gemini, Claude and Nemotron per query
- Search-native intelligence: built for accurate, cited information
- Scheduled Tasks run unattended in the cloud on hourly, daily, weekly or monthly cadences
- Effort mode (Light to Ultra) controls how deeply the model reasons and how many credits it uses
- Portable Computer (local inference, a separate product from the Personal Computer desktop app) runs on supported NVIDIA hardware with local files and no credit consumption
- Authenticated integrations with Gmail, Outlook, GitHub, Linear, Slack, Notion and more


#### Pros


- Starts at $20/mo (Pro), far below the $100 dots floor
- Model flexibility means you're not locked to one provider's output quality
- Tasks pause rather than cancel when credits run out. Work resumes automatically once credits are available
- Personal Computer desktop app gives local file access on Mac and Windows


#### Cons


- Pro plan includes no monthly credits, only weekly Computer usage. Credits for deeper tasks require purchase or a Max plan at $200/mo
- Credit consumption is unpredictable for complex tasks. Heavy or Ultra-effort work can run through a budget quickly
- Effort mode is not available in the macOS and Windows desktop apps
- Answers with confidence even when the underlying sources are thin


#### Pricing


- [$20/mo](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/pricing) (Pro, individual, monthly), weekly Computer usage included, no monthly credits
- **$167/mo** (Max, billed annually), 10,000 credits/month
- **$200/mo** (Max, billed monthly), 10,000 credits/month


#### User Reviews


Perplexity holds a[4.4 out of 5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/perplexity/reviews) from 360 reviews. People praise two things: how fast the research is, and that every claim comes with its source. The ones doing deep research say it makes them look prepared in half the time.


> "[Very clean and easy](https://www.g2.com/products/perplexity/reviews) to work with. The deep research is also pretty fast and accurate."
>
>
> User on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/perplexity/reviews)


#### Best For


I'd pick Perplexity Computer when cited research in every answer is non-negotiable. Per-query model selection and a source on every answer are what set it apart from the other managed agents on this list.


**vs OpenAI Dots:** Dots runs on one model. Perplexity Computer picks the best one for each query and lets you set a preferred one. Both run tasks in the background, and every Perplexity answer comes with its sources.


---


### 5. Gemini Spark: OpenAI Dots alternative for personal Google accounts


Your work already lives in Gmail, Calendar and Drive, and you want an agent that runs there without a plugin layer between the two.[Gemini Spark](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/) connects natively with Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, YouTube and Google Maps, and keeps running 24/7 in the background even when your phone and laptop are off. Define Skills for repeated instructions and Schedules for time-based or conditional triggers, and Spark handles the automation without you setting it up twice.


#### Key Features


- 24/7 background operation, including when phone and laptop are off
- Connections to Google Workspace apps including Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Keep and Tasks
- Skills define reusable instructions for things you do often. Schedules set time or conditional triggers
- Can browse the web via local Chrome or a remote browser in the cloud
- Supports third-party Connected Apps including Dropbox, Zillow, Canva and Instacart
- Up to 15 tasks running simultaneously


#### Pros


- Starts at $19.99/mo (Google AI Pro), well below the $100 dots floor
- Deep Workspace integration means no glue layer between your agent and your work files
- No coding required. Plain conversation is the interface


#### Cons


- Not available in the EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland or the UK, which overlaps with the dots Pro restriction (EEA, Switzerland and the UK)
- Experimental feature in early development: requires supervision and can take unintended actions
- Personal Google Accounts only. Not available on work or school accounts
- If you cancel or downgrade, schedules are paused and access to Spark is lost
- Detailed multi-step analysis still needs a human check and accuracy on complex queries can fall short


#### Pricing


- [$19.99/mo](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/) (Google AI Pro, monthly), Gemini Spark access
- **$99.99/mo** (Google AI Ultra, 5x tier), higher usage limits
- **$199.99/mo** (Google AI Ultra, 20x tier), highest usage limits


#### User Reviews


Gemini holds a[4.4 out of 5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/google-gemini/reviews) from 628 reviews. Most users are on Google Workspace, and what they praise is the time saved on document-heavy work: PDF analysis, spreadsheet scripting and report summaries that took hours and now take minutes.


> "[Performance-wise, the streaming response](https://www.g2.com/products/google-gemini/reviews) speed is blazing fast and has drastically improved my workflow; instead of spending an entire afternoon manually combing through 80-page PDF reports or debugging multi-file Python scripts, I can drop them straight into the chat and get the exact functions and answers I need in seconds, easily saving me 6 to 8 hours each week."
>
>
> User on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/google-gemini/reviews)


#### Best For


Your work runs in Gmail, Calendar and Drive, you want a background agent that operates there natively, and cross-platform reach is not the point. At a fifth of the dots price, Gemini Spark is where I'd go when a personal Google account is already your stack and you don't want a plugin layer sitting between the agent and your files.


**vs OpenAI Dots:** Gemini Spark is missing from the same regions as dots on Pro (and from Nigeria), so it doesn't solve that problem. I'd pick it over dots when your work genuinely lives in Gmail, Calendar and Drive on a personal Google account and native integration matters more than a broader app reach.


---


### 6. Claude Cowork: OpenAI Dots alternative for document and knowledge work


[Claude Cowork](https://claude.com/product/cowork) handles non-coding knowledge work: research, analysis, document creation and multi-step tasks. It runs the same agentic architecture as Claude Code, without a terminal in sight. Give it a goal, it works across the files and tools you specify, and you come back to polished output.


Sessions run in the cloud on Anthropic's servers inside an isolated environment and keep going even after you close your laptop. The built-in browser handles web tasks in the Cowork side panel, separate from your own tabs.


#### Key Features


- Runs on the same agentic architecture as Claude Code, no terminal needed
- Built-in browser in the side panel for opening sites, reading pages, clicking and filling forms
- Sub-agent coordination breaks complex work into parallel workstreams
- Produces Excel spreadsheets with working formulas, PowerPoint presentations and formatted documents
- Scheduled recurring tasks run unattended in the cloud
- Supports plugins that bundle skills, connectors and sub-agents into one install


#### Pros


- Starts at $17/mo (Pro, annual), well below the $100 dots floor
- Available on desktop, web and mobile. Sessions follow you across devices
- Deletion protection requires explicit permission before any files are permanently deleted


#### Cons


- Agentic tasks consume more usage capacity than regular chat. The Pro plan's limits run down faster with Cowork
- Session sharing is not supported. Individual artifacts can be shared but not the session itself
- Cloud sessions on Team and Enterprise plans are in beta. The desktop app adds local file access that web and mobile can't reach


#### Pricing


- [$17/mo](https://claude.com/product/cowork) (Pro, annual, $200 billed up front), Cowork included
- **$20/mo** (Pro, monthly), Cowork included
- **$100/mo** (Max 5x), more usage
- **$200/mo** (Max 20x), highest individual usage


#### User Reviews


Claude holds a[4.6 out of 5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/claude-2025-12-11/reviews) from 485 reviews. The people who use it most describe a full ecosystem: code work in Claude Code, delegated multi-step tasks in Cowork, research and brainstorming in Claude Chat. The thing that keeps coming up is having all of it in one place.


> "[I use Claude Code](https://www.g2.com/products/claude-2025-12-11/reviews) for coding and navigating codebases, Cowork for delegating tasks and getting multi-step work done, and Claude Chat for research, design, brainstorming, and general problem-solving. Having all of these capabilities in one ecosystem has made a real difference in how I approach my work."
>
>
> User on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/claude-2025-12-11/reviews)


#### Best For


You'd want Cowork when the day is research, analysis and document creation rather than system admin or role management. If that's the shape of your work, it runs inside a product you probably already trust.


**vs OpenAI Dots:** Both run cloud tasks in the background. Cowork is built specifically for non-coding knowledge work and document output. Dots is a generalist.


---


### 7. Lindy: OpenAI Dots alternative for event-triggered workflows


A trigger starts a routine in Lindy: an email arrives, a meeting ends, a Slack message appears, and Lindy acts. It reaches 1,500+ integrations including Gmail, Slack, Notion and HubSpot (plus MCP support), ships with 40+ built-in skills covering research, data analysis, decks and dashboards, and lets teams save their own. Approval is required before any action with outside impact, and your data is never used to train models.


Credits are pooled at the workspace level, where admins can cap how much any one person pulls.


#### Key Features

## OpenAI Dots head-to-head: Grok Bot and Marblism compared


Two tools in this roster are worth comparing directly against dots: Grok Bot because it is the closest hosted match, Marblism because it takes the opposite approach.


### OpenAI Dots vs Grok Bot


Both are persistent cloud agents that run 24/7, connect to tools and handle tasks in the background, and both keep approval decisions for risky actions with you. The difference is ecosystem and how isolation works.


Dots lives inside ChatGPT and plugs into over 4,000 apps through OpenAI's plugin network. Each dot gets its own isolated cloud computer.


Grok Bot lives inside Cursor's ecosystem and plugs into the same MCP servers, plugins and skills as Cursor. All your bots share 1 persistent cloud computer, isolated per user rather than per bot. The on-demand token cost is the thing to watch.


**Pick OpenAI Dots if:** you're already inside ChatGPT's ecosystem and want the plugin reach with no additional setup.


**Pick Grok Bot if:** you're in Cursor or SuperGrok, you want an agent that enters at $20/mo (Cursor Pro), or you want bots that can hand work off to each other through a shared cloud computer.


### OpenAI Dots vs Marblism


Dots and Marblism both take work off your plate, but they split it differently.


A working week with Marblism: you hand each AI Employee its role, it works from one shared record of the business, and nothing goes out until you approve it. A working week with dots: you direct each agent toward a task, it runs on OpenAI's cloud, and you pick it back up when it pings you. Marblism at $24 a month on the yearly plan covers seven roles. A dot starts at $100 a month.


Stop paying for Marblism and the roles stop, but every output you approved stays with you. OpenAI's page doesn't say what you keep if you stop paying for the plan. Marblism has no region restriction on the product itself (Rachel's local phone numbers cover the US, Canada, the UK, Mexico and Australia). Dots on a Pro plan does. Every Marblism action waits for your sign-off before it goes out.


**Pick OpenAI Dots if:** you want a single generalist agent you can direct toward any task and you're already on a Pro plan.


**Pick Marblism if:** you want specific business roles handled without directing an agent through each one, or the $100 dots floor is more than you want to spend.

## When OpenAI Dots is worth the price


Three situations where I'd stay with dots, price and region restriction included.


### Proactive background research on a managed cloud computer


Every dot gets a sandboxed cloud environment, and when you aren't actively working with it, it runs proactive background research using read-only tools. Those tools can't send messages, change app content or control your browser or computer during background research. Auto-review checks risky actions against your instructions and safety requirements before they execute. If you want a genuinely always-on research agent with clear guardrails, the architecture holds up.


### Over 4000 apps inside ChatGPT from the first dot


The first dot is included in your Pro or Business Premium plan, and from day one it connects to over 4,000 apps through OpenAI's plugin ecosystem, which already lives inside ChatGPT. If you live in ChatGPT and your tools are already there, dots drops its agent layer on top without any migration.

Business Premium users get access across all supported ChatGPT regions. If the EEA, UK, or Switzerland restriction is blocking you on Pro, Business Premium at $100 per seat per month (annual, 2-seat workspace minimum) removes it and adds 5x more usage than a Standard seat with no 5-hour usage limit. For teams that need dots and are in those regions, that's the path forward.

A dot runs 24/7 on its own cloud computer, takes actions in real tools (files, apps, the web), and keeps working between conversations. A chatbot waits for a prompt within a session and responds to it.

### Privacy and setup for OpenAI Dots


#### Can I run an OpenAI Dots alternative on my own computer?


Yes, for OpenClaw, Hermes Agent and OpenDots. OpenClaw installs on macOS and Linux via a one-liner and runs on Windows too. Its macOS desktop app needs macOS 15 or later. Hermes Agent has a desktop app for macOS 12+ and Windows 10/11. OpenDots requires Node.js 24 and npm. OpenClaw and Hermes Agent run on hardware you control with no subscription required. OpenDots needs CopilotKit Intelligence for conversations, and its free Developer plan covers a renewable 30-day evaluation license.


#### Does a dot share my credentials across OpenAI's systems?


A dot's own context does not retain credentials, images or screenshots. When signing into supported websites, a dot can use saved passwords without passing them to the model. Each dot runs in its own sandboxed environment, isolated from other users' cloud environments. Sensitive tasks like changing a password stay with you.


#### Does deleting a dot delete my files?


When you delete a dot, its context goes with it: conversations, saved memories and scheduled tasks. Files, Codex threads and ChatGPT conversations the dot created are stored separately and stay intact.
